record.original_question: What is the general form of fractional integrals and fractional derivatives for functions defined on a finite interval when those operators are required to satisfy the desiderata HL1-HL6 that formalize the expected algebraic and limiting behavior of fractional calculus operators?

evidence.quote: The families of the operators I^alpha, alpha >= 0 and D^alpha, alpha >= 0 can be interpreted as fractional integrals and fractional derivatives, respectively, if they satisfy the following six properties (called desiderata in [30]).
Deduce a general form of the fractional integrals and derivatives for the functions defined on a finite interval in the sense of the desiderata formulated in the previous section.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a finite interval and consider, on a suitable space of real- or complex-valued functions defined on $[a,b]$, two one-parameter families of linear operators
$$\{I^{\alpha}\}_{\alpha\ge 0},\qquad \{D^{\alpha}\}_{\alpha\ge 0},$$
which are intended to play the roles of "fractional integral" and "fractional derivative" of order $\alpha$, respectively. Require that these families satisfy the following six desiderata:

(HL1) $I^{0}=D^{0}=\mathrm{Id}$ (the identity operator).

(HL2) $I^{1}$ coincides with the ordinary definite integration operator $f\mapsto \int_{a}^{x} f(t)\,dt$, and $D^{1}$ coincides with the ordinary derivative $\dfrac{d}{dx}$ (on appropriate domains).

(HL3) Index law for the integrals: $I^{\alpha}\,I^{\beta}=I^{\alpha+\beta}$ for all $\alpha,\beta\ge 0$.

(HL4) The derivative is a left inverse of the integral: $D^{\alpha}\,I^{\alpha}=\mathrm{Id}$ for all $\alpha\ge 0$.

(HL5) Continuity (in an appropriate topology) of the families with respect to the order $\alpha$, including the limiting behavior $I^{\alpha}\to\mathrm{Id}$ and $D^{\alpha}\to\mathrm{Id}$ as $\alpha\to 0^{+}$.

(HL6) An appropriate generalized Fundamental Theorem of Fractional Calculus connecting $I^{\alpha}$ and $D^{\alpha}$ on the chosen function spaces.

Problem: Determine the most general form of the operator families $\{I^{\alpha}\}_{\alpha\ge 0}$ and $\{D^{\alpha}\}_{\alpha\ge 0}$ acting on functions defined on the finite interval $[a,b]$ such that all six desiderata (HL1)–(HL6) are satisfied. In particular, characterize the admissible kernels (and the associated function spaces) for which such left- and right-sided fractional integrals and derivatives can be constructed, and exhibit their explicit representation.
artifact.category_tag: general fractional calculus on a finite interval
artifact.status_search_result: A 2023 paper by Luchko, "The General Fractional Integrals and Derivatives on a Finite Interval" (Mathematics 11(4), 1031), introduces left- and right-sided general fractional integrals and derivatives on a finite interval using Sonine-type kernel sets (Luchko/Kochubei sets) and develops their fundamental theorem, providing a substantial answer to the problem in this kernel-based framework. A fully general classification under all six desiderata HL1–HL6 in maximal generality does not appear to be definitively closed, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The General Fractional Integrals and Derivatives on a Finite Interval
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces general fractional integrals and derivatives of functions on a finite interval, with both left- and right-sided operators, using Sonine-type kernel sets.
status_evidence.claim: A general construction of fractional integrals and derivatives on a finite interval, satisfying analogues of the desiderata, has been developed, providing a partial answer.

status_evidence.title: Desiderata for Fractional Derivatives and Integrals
status_evidence.snippet: Hilfer and Luchko propose desiderata characterizing what should be called a fractional integral or derivative.
status_evidence.claim: The desiderata HL1–HL6 referenced in the problem originate in the Hilfer–Luchko framework.
